name: Ambiguous: make shortened URLs more secure
whyThisType: The requirement names a goal, not a change. Input validation, authentication, rate limiting and short-code entropy are different changes with different risks, so any autonomous choice would be a guess.
clarificationQuestion: "Secure" can mean several different changes here. Which security improvement is intended: (a) rejecting unsafe URL schemes / requiring valid http(s) destinations, (b) authenticating the management API, (c) rate limiting redirects, or (d) making short codes unguessable? Please state the intended behaviour.
exampleHumanAnswer: Reject unsafe URL schemes and require HTTP or HTTPS URLs with a valid host.

expectedGraphVersionTransition.note: Version 1 stays persisted and queryable via GET /api/workflows/{id}/graph?version=1; replanning adds a version, it never overwrites one.

expectedOrchestrationBehaviour: Before codebase-analysis the clarification gate recognises the ambiguity.
The workflow is parked in AWAITING_CLARIFICATION with a persisted question.
A CLARIFICATION decision records why the orchestrator stopped instead of guessing.
A human answers via POST /api/workflows/{id}/clarifications/{clarificationId}/answer with replan=true.
The answer becomes the requirement text and graph version 2 is created; the run returns to READY.
A REPLAN decision and REPLAN_STARTED/GRAPH_CREATED/REPLAN_COMPLETED audit events record the lineage.
Version 2 is started by a human and runs to completion under the clarified requirement.

expectedOutcomeOfVersion2.codebaseAnalysis: Records that the clarified behaviour already exists in url-shortener-service (UrlValidator + ShortUrlService.create + HTTP 400 handling).
expectedOutcomeOfVersion2.implementation: Records 'no code change required' rather than duplicating the existing validation.
expectedOutcomeOfVersion2.note: The scenario demonstrates ambiguity handling, clarification, replanning, history and controlled autonomy. It does not claim the validation feature was invented now - it already existed in the baseline, and discovering that is the point.

expectedAffectedComponents: reused unchanged: ClarificationService, ReplanService, GovernanceWorkflowService, AuditService
validationExpectations: The raw ambiguous requirement does not run to completion autonomously.
A clarification request is persisted and readable via the API.
The supplied answer is persisted with its author.
Replanning creates graph version 2 while version 1 stays queryable.
Decision and audit lineage explain why the plan changed.
Version 2 runs to COMPLETED under the clarified requirement.
An unambiguous requirement is never parked by the gate.

tests: orchestrator-service: AmbiguityDetectorTest (only known ambiguity patterns trigger)
orchestrator-service: AmbiguousRequirementScenarioIntegrationTest (end-to-end park -> answer -> replan -> v2 completes)
orchestrator-service: ClarificationGateIntegrationTest and ReplanIntegrationTest (the reused mechanisms)

intentionalBoundaries: Ambiguity detection is a short, explicit list of known phrasings - not a general requirement classifier.
Unambiguous requirements are never parked, so the gate does not become a permanent stop.
The question is asked at most once per workflow: answering it releases the run, it never loops.
The orchestrator never picks an interpretation on its own.
